Text: Can you describe the smelliest person you have met? Some months ago I was on the bus headed homewards. One of my pleasures in life is being able to read leisurely without any disturbance whilst on the typically quiet journey home on such bus. But alas, on that very day, such was not in the cards for me. Not by a longshot. The biggest chatterbox I know in existence happened to come into the bus and sat directly opposite me prodding me on the shoulder while I sat with headphones on attempting to read. I groaned but extended courtesy towards listening and engaging in some small talk about her workplace gossip, family gossip, how great her husband is, how she feels about bla bla bla. Nothing is wrong with all this except that she is one of those rare individuals who doesn't allow the talk to falter and prods you with a barrage of inane questions as though to ensure she has your complete attention. While trying to evade some rather nosy and trifling questions I got a whiff of of a scent that can only be described as startlingly ominous. I grimaced a bit and stared suspiciously at my acquaintance and nervously took a moderate whiff to determine if she was the culprit. Thankfully she wasn't. I was wondering if was just a fluke scent that drafted temporarily from the netherregion of some coarse individual who had left the bus but the scent happened to linger on for some seconds longer. I told myself the scent was gone. But alas, like a slap in the face the scent struck me again. It was even more powerful this time. Even through my facemask I could smell the scent, a scent that could only be described as something so offensive that it was beyond bestial. It smelt as though someone rubbed a sweaty, boozy armpit against my nose and then held my face upon the taint of some scoundrel who refused to bathe for weeks. 'Are you smelling that?’ I asked Madame Chatterbox and she stared at me with a rather dumb smile and replied, 'Smelling what?’ There was a pause and she continued with her monologue interspersed with trivial questionings. I began to get a headache. Someone in the back stank the high hell but I couldn't determine who was the culprit. There was a security officer, a middle aged woman and a sleeping old man in the back. None of them looked like the kind of person whose power of stench could bring the dead back to life. The scent came in waves; faintly menacing at its best, repugnant at its worst. So as not to retch I had to practice breathing through my mouth, but I felt nauseous knowing that I was sucking in that toxic air through my mouth and into my lungs. Madame Chatterbox continued on, despite the natural disaster that occured right in front of her nose. 'I'm so tired. I could just drop on my bed and sleep until next Monday. But I have to cook for my husband. You know how hard it is to cook every evening? You cook? I'm sure you probably go out and buy food every day. Lucky you.’ I didn't know what was worse. Having to endure that scent or having to endure Chatterbox's prying and passive aggressive vents disguised as small talk. Whatever poison was worse, the combination of the two was like a hellish torture. I was hoping at some bus stop, whomsoever was the culprit would hop off the bus. Hardly anyone ever went as far as the final stop. It would usually be just me and (unfortunately) Madame Chatterbox. At mid point the middle aged lady left the bus. At three quarter point the security guard hopped off. The only person left was the sleeping old man. Funny thing was, he didn't look like someone who would smell like a modern day torture instrument. He was relatively well dressed and ordinary looking. Another funny thing was I never saw him in the bus nor in the village before. He was a complete stranger. He lay snoring unwares as to the destruction that lay manifest under his arms and amidst his much unattended nether regions. I felt such a rage at his stink at some point I wanted to grab him by the collar, drag him to the front by the driver and demand that the driver smell him and agree to kick him out the bus. But alas such would not be the case. Mr. Smelly stayed with us the entire journey and Madame Chatterbox squawked the entire trip until I was rendered temporarily disabled by a pounding headache. When Mr. Smelly awoke and saw the final stop he bolted upright and shouted to the driver that he was on the wrong bus. He ran to the driver and begged that he remain on the bus to head back where it came from. The driver, finally getting a whiff of the scent, roared for the man to exit the bus immediately. While we exited the bus I could hear Mr. Smelly drunkenly complain that someone could have woken him up and told him he was on the wrong bus. He would've stoppped off much earlier and head back to the bus station. Hearing him say that and acknowledging the fact that all the torture was unnecessary, made me want to walk up to him and murder him. But alas such was not to happen.

The biggest chatterbox I know in existence happened to come into the bus and sat directly opposite me prodding me on the shoulder while I sat with headphones on attempting to read. I groaned but extended courtesy towards listening and engaging in some small talk about her workplace gossip, family gossip, how great her husband is, how she feels about bla bla bla. Nothing is wrong with all this except that she is one of those rare individuals who doesn't allow the talk to falter and prods you with a barrage of inane questions as though to ensure she has your complete attention. While trying to evade some rather nosy and trifling questions I got a whiff of of a scent that can only be described as startlingly ominous. I grimaced a bit and stared suspiciously at my acquaintance and nervously took a moderate whiff to determine if she was the culprit. Thankfully she wasn't. I was wondering if was just a fluke scent that drafted temporarily from the netherregion of some coarse individual who had left the bus but the scent happened to linger on for some seconds longer. I told myself the scent was gone. But alas, like a slap in the face the scent struck me again. It was even more powerful this time. Even through my facemask I could smell the scent, a scent that could only be described as something so offensive that it was beyond bestial. It smelt as though someone rubbed a sweaty, boozy armpit against my nose and then held my face upon the taint of some scoundrel who refused to bathe for weeks. 'Are you smelling that?\u2019 I asked Madame Chatterbox and she stared at me with a rather dumb smile and replied, 'Smelling what?\u2019 There was a pause and she continued with her monologue interspersed with trivial questionings. I began to get a headache. Someone in the back stank the high hell but I couldn't determine who was the culprit. There was a security officer, a middle aged woman and a sleeping old man in the back. None of them looked like the kind of person whose power of stench could bring the dead back to life. The scent came in waves; faintly menacing at its best, repugnant at its worst. So as not to retch I had to practice breathing through my mouth, but I felt nauseous knowing that I was sucking in that toxic air through my mouth and into my lungs. Madame Chatterbox continued on, despite the natural disaster that occured right in front of her nose. 'I'm so tired. I could just drop on my bed and sleep until next Monday. But I have to cook for my husband. You know how hard it is to cook every evening? You cook? I'm sure you probably go out and buy food every day. Lucky you.\u2019 I didn't know what was worse. Whatever poison was worse, the combination of the two was like a hellish torture. I was hoping at some bus stop, whomsoever was the culprit would hop off the bus. But alas such would not be the case. Mr. Smelly stayed with us the entire journey and Madame Chatterbox squawked the entire trip until I was rendered temporarily disabled by a pounding headache. He ran to the driver and begged that he remain on the bus to head back where it came from. The driver, finally getting a whiff of the scent, roared for the man to exit the bus immediately. Text: What’s the most unprofessional thing a doctor has said to you? Thing? You mean things. If you trust the word of just one doctor here in Trinidad you already have one foot (or in our case, leg) in the grave. My ex and I witnessed the not so great morals and ethics of some of the private health care 'professionals’ in Trinidad after she developed a severe case of cellulitis. This developed after she suffered a cut from a dirty galvanize sheet a neighbor had lying about in the road. This is how it looked after a month of healing. You don’t want to see what it looked like when it was critical. The disrespectful and dishonest negligence of the doctors who treated her was far worse than the actual injury. Left up to them, she could’ve lost her leg or gotten blood poisoning and die. So what did the doctors do/say? Here’s what happened: The cut looked minor so she decided to ignore it. A few days later an infection spreads around it the size of closed fist and it burns her all day. She had the typical Trini mindset that the public hospitals were were no good so I took her to a private doctor her relatives recommended. Said doctor diagnosed the infection as a mild case of cellulitis, gives her a prescription for some weak pills and sends us off. A week later the infection spreads to the size of a man’s foot and it burns even more severely. In panic we visit another private doctor and he tells us something to the extent of: ‘It’s just a minor infection. It’s just running its course.’ He bandages her leg and prescribes her the same medication like the last doctor. He bashes the last doctor for not bandaging her leg. We return to the old doctor to give him a piece of our mind and get our money back. His curmudgeonous, old secretary tells us that the doctor is busy. We show her the extent to which the infection has spread and she replies: ‘So what? It’s not like her leg is rotten.’ Tempted to choke slam the old bitch I take my rage out on the door and in a mad fury I threaten that I would come back to smear s**t all over his office building during the night…..because that what they really were. We place our trust in the second doctor and visit him weekly even though all he does is re-bandage her leg and prescribe the same medicine. He keeps assuring us that cellulitis is common and non-threatening, not to worry. At this point the infection has spread throughout her entire leg. The new doctor is collecting a neat $500 from me for each visit. By the third visit, he unwraps the old bandages and I literally see him gulp in shock as he witnesses the extent of the infection. I’ll never forget the cheap smile on the smug face as he tries to play it off coolly by saying: ‘Ok……it seems to have spread a bit. Maybe if I prescribe a stronger medication?’ That was when I realized the scheme. Some private doctors make their wealth by prolonging the ailment. Took her immediately to our Mt. Hope public hospital where she was confined for several days. The doctor there told her that if we had continued in the manner in which we treated the situation, best case scenario would’ve been an amputated leg. I shuddered when she recalled to me those words. I can only imagine the amount of lives lost due to selfish, negligent doctors looking to profit off of people’s misfortunes. The scar remains on her leg, not as prominent, but as a subtle reminder to a) Do not take any injury for granted, regardless how minor. b) Just because it’s private i.e. non Governmental, doesn’t mean it’s better. Edit 21.01.22. Sorry if this answer was a bit depressing. Have you ever been depressed? I survived a really bad spell myself. Thankfully I lived through it and was lucky that it was not clinical. Click here to read all about it.

Text: Why do women *hate* nerdy men? When I was coming into my teens I was a proper nerd. I was obsessed with Japanese anime, foreign films, the 60s and the psychedelic rock of the period. When I wasn't writing my pompous and psudo-artsy short stories I was spending hours behind the PlayStation and computer playing video games. When I wasn't watching late night soft-core porn on Cinemax I was delighting in clips from the Classical Arts Showcase channel. I would rant and vent about how awful the girls in my school were to the girls in my school. I would find solace in the public library where I scoured the building looking for that quiet, introverted pretty young girl(s) from an all girls school and would proceed to sit next to her(them) without asking permission and then I would gush about my unfinished surreal novel about a country boy in my class having trouble deciphering dreams from reality and vice versa. These girls would find me mildly amusing and interesting but I didn't seem to understand that 'Sorry my parents don't allow me to give out our phone number is actually a diplomatic way of saying no. (This was before cell phones were a thing.) Yes I was a nerd. A big nerd. I still am. However girls didn't hate the nerd in me. What they didn't like was that: Those are traits that are signs of possible narcissists, self-centred a**holes, crybabies and sociopaths. Not that I was any of the above it’s just that those are the type of men girls really *hate* and even fear. Not nerds so much.

Text: What movies have you judged just by looking at their posters? Something about this poster just rubbed me the wrong way. Is that a movie or a shot of the celebrity audience during the last Academy Awards? At first glance it looks like the typical dime-a-dozen Hollywood movie poster. The kind of movie poster that would fleetingly catch your fancy if you're late to the cinema and the movie you wanted to watch is sold out. But when you actually sit and and digest the vision before you, you might be like me and notice it has ALL the trappings of a tepid Hollywood wannabe blockbuster. The poster seems to scream several things to you all at once: Despite the little information that is given, you have an idea of what the gist of the movie is about. None of the above posters are hiding their story behind a montage of A-list faces. All the above posters are proud of their story and want you to know what you are paying to see. Either through clever visuals or teasing, enigmatic catch phrases, you have an idea whether this movie is your cup of tea or not. Let's take a look at the poster for Don't Look Up one last time. That’s just rancid. Adam McKay and his major studio goons insult my intelligence by telling me that I'm too stupid to understand satire so rather than waste time hinting what the story is about, here are a bunch of eye pleasing celebrities…..and it's inspired by stuff that might kinda happen. I'm not gonna see this movie based on this poster. I might be missing the greatest film of the 21st century but I'll trust my intuition on this one. Edit 10.01.22. Geez, what an awful poster. Do you judge a movie by its poster? Click here to see my pick of the greatest and worst movie poster I’ve ever seen.

Text: What is the lowest probability event you have personally witnessed? I did a degree in Agribusiness when I attended University. Nutrition and Dietetics students shared the Faculty with us and among the students of N&D was a guy named Gandhi. Gandhi was a short, portly and ambiguously gay chatterbox. He was exceptionally kind and friendly but he loved to have long frivolous conversations that ranged from anything from popular soap operas to university gossip. As an evening student most of my classmates were, oddly enough, middle-aged working women, many of them single mothers and a few of them were grandmothers. Gandhi would come over to our area and chat with us and many of these ladies took an instant liking to him. I, on the other hand, found him a bit too loud, clingy and as mentioned earlier frivolous. One day, my fellow Agribusiness students and I were waiting for a bus. We were to go on a cross country field trip. Gandhi was hanging out with us while we waited and being his usual loud and silly self. One of the students didn't show up so there was room for one on the bus. Gandhi speculated whether the lecturer would allow him to come on the trip even though he wasn't an Agribusiness student. When the bus arrived with the lecturer, Gandhi’s lady friends immediately begged for him to be allowed on the trip. Through chance Gandhi got a seat next to me and from the moment the bus took off and the 6 hrs that followed Gandhi yapped his mouth non-stop. Kind and affable, the lecturer said that since he was in the same faculty he couldn't see it being a problem since there was room for one more. We all boarded the bus. Through chance Gandhi got a seat next to me and from the moment the bus took off and the 6 hrs that followed Gandhi yapped his mouth non-stop. I could not enjoy a single moment of silence to enjoy the sights and sounds with this silly, little man next to me going off on every irrelevant topic that a human could think of during a cross country road trip. To say that my experience was somewhat diminished would be an understatement. Two years after graduating from university my aunt invites me to a trip to Dominica organized by a forestry conservation group. The conservation group was, oddly enough, comprised mostly of middle-aged women and a few grandmothers. On the first day we were to go to a cross country trip on a bus around the little island. Some of the group had opted out of the trip in favour of doing some shopping in the capital Roseau or just relaxing in the hotel. As such I had a seat free to myself next to me. While the bus was driving I was reminded of the cross country trip with Gandhi. The bus driver first took us to the the nearest shops for those who still needed to purchase drinks or snacks. We all went into a little grocery. While browsing the shelves I almost froze when I heard a familiar voice. \u2018Elijah?\u2019 it said, \u2018What are you doing in Dominica?\u2019 I turned around to see none other than Gandhi himself, like a portly imp-genie who manifests himself whenever one thought about him. We have room.\u2019 \u2018No f**king way,\u2019 I told myself. Filing back into the bus I hoped to God one of the group members would decide to sit next to me this time. I eyed them all down as they entered, with warm looks, in the vain hope that they change their previous seat and sit to my side, preventing Gandhi from sitting next to me once again. As per fate, that was not to be. Gandhi was the last to enter the bus. He saw my empty seat and immediately sat next to me. I stared at him in a state of wonder and disbelief. I was expecting him to feel the same way. Text: What's your take on Imane Khelif, a biologically proven male boxer, taking part in the Women's Boxing event at the Paris Olympics 2024? I feel sorry for Imane Khelif. The problem is she premiered in the Olympics at the time when the whole trans women in sports became a hugely divisive and contentious issue, all thanks to this idiot. Inane Khelif has a unique makeup in terms of her gender but was born a female with female genitalia. There was no sex change involved. She is not a man nor a tran. She is just a somewhat masculine woman. Some people don’t realize that she is also someone with feelings. This is the first thing Imane Khelif did after the fight. Look at that photo and tell me you don’t see the face of someone deeply concerned about her opponent. Angela Carini refused to shake Khelif’s hand after her defeat. Carini claimed that Khelif punched harder than anything she felt from any other opponent. She refused to even look Khelif in the face. No one seems to take into regard Khelif is a human being with feelings and that she is now looked upon by the world as some sort of freak before she is even given a chance to speak her story. I am as conservative as they get but in this case I think we are being nothing more than bullies. I have news for people who are angry and want Khelif banished simply because she looks masculine; female boxers/close combat fighters tend to look masculine, in case we’ve forgotten Even Carini has apologized about her post fight comments. Trans women in biological women’s sport is indeed an issue that I’m against but let us not drag Imane Khelif into this ugly fight. She has to take physical blows for a living. It’s not fair that she has to get emotional blows as well.

Text: Has your friend ever saved your life? Well he's my cousin but he's also my friend. Ten years ago my cousin Keeghan and I were staying at his family's beach house. Feeling idle we decided to roam the empty beach an early morning, light cherry bombs and fling them in random directions. The beach (Las Cuevas) was long and we walked the entire length towards the west. It ended at some cliffs and we spotted a large smooth surfaced rock several feet from the shore. I watched as my 6′5 cousin swam to it and climbed to the top. I immediately followed suit. However my luck was it that strong winds had the waves lashing against the rock generating some strong, swirling undercurrents. As I reached towards the rock I felt the undercurrent pull me downwards, spun me around and flung me upwards. I laughed it off and so did Keeghan. He said I looked like a lump of shit being flushed. As I began laughing the undercurrent pulled me down again and kept me swirling underwater. I had to utilize energy to avoid slamming into the rock while being tossed around. As hard as I tried to break out of the swirling undercurrents it was too strong and I only managed to tire myself out. Keeghan saw that I was beginning to gurgle and lose energy, it was only a matter of time before I drowned. He jumped into the water in an area where the water wasn't swirling and being blessed with a long frame he was able to easily reach me and pull me out of the undercurrent. We laughed it off and he played it like no big deal but I knew that I would've been dead if it wasn't for him.

Text: Have you ever had a life-changing experience while working in fast food? Right now in Trinidad, there is a growing stigma and stereotype of Venezuelan people. After the massive exodus of Venezuelan migrants following the country’s epic breakdown, Trinidad has had its fair share of migrants. Watching YouTube videos of empty groceries, families eating out of garbage cans, theft, riots etc. Many of our hearts went out to the suffering people and wanted to help as best as we could these poor people going through such tragedy. When the first wave of migrants landed we looked on with bated breath, expecting to scores of people looking like this: and this Instead, what many of saw was mostly this: It was a shock that instead of seeing scared and underfed families grateful for help and a new start in life, many of us instead saw plump, well-dressed, somewhat cocky young men and women parading about the towns, enjoying nightlife, shopping away merrily and just living it up as though the crisis in Venezuela was just a fairy tale. It is not uncommon to see a young Venezuelan couple walking the streets wearing sneakers that are valued more than the average Trini’s monthly salary. On a daily basis one would see men and women who never wore the same outfit twice, pedicured hands, gold watches, necklaces and earrings, Ray-Ban shades and ordering fast food religiously. It was a shock to see many of them indulging in such a costly lifestyle after the economic ruin of their country. It seemed that the people we believed we were saving from starvation were flaunting a high-end lifestyle that many of us wouldn’t dare try to emulate. Were these Venezuelas refugees or tourists? How could they support themselves in the long run with such a lifestyle? Why don't they save their money? This was, of course, not the case for all of the migrants. There were families who adopted humble lifestyles and tried their best to be inconspicuous. Unfortunately these families were rarely seen. The working adults simply went to work and back home while the rest of the family remained indoors, staying out of trouble. I suggested that I ride to the bakery and get her brother’s key. She didn't want me to get in trouble at work but I shushed her and let her use my phone to make a call to her brother. When she started speaking Spanish I was startled: we spoke English for so long that I forgot for a moment that she was a Venezuelan. Phantasm (1979) This movie is infuriatingly odd in that in one light it is a genius work of art with its surreal aesthetics, bizarre yet original concept and villain yet in another light it's a piece of trash. It's all thanks to the horrid, nauseating screenplay by the director Don Coscarelli. If anyone should get ‘A for Effort, D for Execution’ engraved on his tombstone, it's Don Coscarelli. The plot for Phantasm concerns Mike, Jody and Reggie who attend a funeral for a friend Tommy (the characters are as bland as their generic names) who was mysteriously murdered. Things get bizarre as they are pursued by a tall, stone-faced man in a suit, deadly, flying, brain drilling silver spheres and hideous dwarfs in medieval monk robes. Clearly this concept came to the director with the aid of some powerful hallucinogens. The film has a eerie yet fascinating visual style, warped time and space narrative and a unique sense of discordance. This is quite possibly the greatest horror movie for stoners and I'm sure that's what attributed to the whopping $22 million it made on a $200,000 budget. But the movie is complete shite if you try to watch it sober for the intrinsic value of its story. Here's why: What a great movie Phantasm would've been if someone more visionary and disciplined like Tim Burton or Elias Merhige (Begotten, Shadow of the Vampire) had directed/scripted the film. Text: What's the biggest anticlimax in movie history? Bird Box (2018) was throughly gripping. All the characters were well fleshed out and relatable and as ridiculous as the premise was (unseen, omnipresent entities that makes one commit suicide if seen) the suspense and horror was so effective it became the most streamed Netflix film at the time, mostly due to word of mouth. SPOILER ALERT But by God what a stupid ending. After so much trauma in the first half of the film, years later Sandra Bullock’s character Malorie and her children (one biological, one adopted) are rowing blindfolded down a dangerous river to find the people who sent her a transmission as to a safe location. After a nail biting odyssey down the river we are all expecting to be given answers when she finally arrives at this mysterious, resistance base. What are those creatures? Where did they come from? What do they want? Why do people kill themselves just by looking at them? What is the state of the world right now? Do the entities have a weakness, is it possible to fight back? Instead the movie does the most dirty tactic that a studio could possible do. Instead of providing the audience what they waited for and dedicated our energy and emotions toward (answers) the studio goes the cheap route and decides to end the film by answering nothing, leaving the film open to sequels and prequels. This is a trend I’ve noticed in a lot of modern horrors and thrillers. They just can't end the effing movie and give us the closure that we waited two hours for. Ranting aside, Malorie reaches the destination, a school for the blind and everyone assures her that everything will be ok in one of the most corniest and cliched endings ever conceived. It’s a pity Malorie didn’t wake up from a dream and see all the familiar faces around her while uttering ‘There’s no place like home.’ I would’ve much appreciated that ending than the actual ending of Bird Box.

Text: What’s your favorite movie based on true events? The Founder (2016) This is a movie I habitually return to watching. It's an inspiring movie but it's not a ‘feelgood’ movie per se. The movie tells the story of how a run of the mill salesman named Ray Kroc outmanoeuvred and outperformed the McDonald brothers and became owner of the McDonald's franchise/empire. I say it's not feelgood because, based on the film, Kroc was not by any account a ‘nice’ man when it came to business. He was a conniving opportunist but at the same time he was also unrelentingly persistent. His partners, the altruistic McDonald brothers derived a brilliant concept and product but had little interest in franchising and/or wealth. It is because of Kroc's persistence and willingness to take great risks that McDonald's is the success that it is today. If there is one concept the movie begs you to take away from it, regardless of your view of Ray Kroc, it is the value of persistence. Without giving away too much of the plot, this is what is inspiring about Kroc's efforts. There are so many profound scenes and quotes in this movie that it find it hard for anyone to not appreciate it for the sole merit that it generates a lot of thought, regardless of whether you don't like it or find Ray Kroc reprehensible. I think Michael Keaton gave his greatest performance and I was thoroughly disappointed that he was not nominated for an Academy Award. His persistence speech at the end of the film, I consider to be a classic in business motivation, trumping that of Jordan Belfort’s ‘sell me this pen’ in The Wolf of Wall Street and Alec Baldwin's ‘Always be closing’ scene in Glengarry Glen Ross. I beg to debate this opinion.

Text: As a teacher, have you ever been accused of something? I'm not a teacher but as a librarian we operate in the role of a teacher sometimes. A student by the name of Keston was in the back of the library, headphones on, singing loudly an explicit rap song complete with excessive use of the n-word, obscene language and misogynistic lyrics. This created a ruckus in the library with some students laughing and others disturbed by his singing. Keston pretended that he was doing schoolwork and not noticing a thing. This grinded my gears. Keston was usually a well-behaved young man but lately he was starting to act up as though desperation for attention. He was of African descent and quite dark skinned. I went over to him and tapped on the table and warned him to stop with the singing. He nodded and I left but the moment I went back to my desk he started singing again, even more loudly, causing the class clowns to bellow in laughter. I went over to him and touched his shoulder. 'Nigger don't touch me' he said and he continued his singing, his clowns rolling in laughter. 'Can you please get out of the library!’ I said calmly and he proceeded to laugh at me and continue singing his vile verses. I asked him one more time to get out of the library otherwise he'd be banned. He proceeded to sing gangster rap lyrics of shooting my bitch-ass full of holes while gesturing pointing a gun at me with his fingers. I then got an idea. 'Keston!’ I said loudly, 'Can you please get your disrespectful black ass out of this library.’ He immediately stopped. His clowns fell silent. I watched as he got worked up called me racist several times and threatened that I would lose my job. In his mind it was okay to call me nigger and gesture shooting me but it was not okay for someone to tell him to get his black ass out. Keston didn't realise that this was Trinidad not the US. Keston then left the library and a few minutes later returned with the School Safety Officer (SSO) Mr. Aigle, a man as dark as himself . Unaware that Aigle and I had a good working relationship, Keston proceeded to recount a story minimizing his actions and emphasising that I shouted violent and racist slogans at him. When I told my side of the story several students confirmed what I had said. I apologized for my choice of words but Aigle told me not to, citing the Golden Rule. He then told Keston to bring his black ass into his office immediately. Aigle was the most un-PC, un-subjective person on the school compound and Keston thought by having the same skin colour, Aigle would have the same mindset as him. Boy was he wrong. He got suspended for a week. I've long since transferred out of that school but if I see old Aigle again I'll get him that beer I promised him.

Text: Why do some people not like Coldplay? As probably the only guy answering this question who actually likes Coldplay I’d like to put forward my theory. There are actually two Coldplays. Old Coldplay Modern Coldplay What is the first thing you noticed about the photos? Old Coldplay shows a young band full of awkward post A-Level graduates who don’t care how geeky they look but seem to enjoy each other’s company and being themselves. Modern Coldplay shows an intensely edited photo of four men who are trying their utmost best to look cool and serious. Everything about the photo screams over saturated, highly commercial and bloated. I sincerely doubt the guys even posed together for the photo but rather had separate photos, photoshopped together. Old Coldplay is alternative rock. Yes they wrote a fair share of ballads. Yes they could be whiny, moody and (as another Quora writer has so artfully suggested) ‘sangfroid’ but there was a meticulous attention to instrumentation and songwriting that you can’t listen to songs like Trouble, Clocks and Shiver and call it pop music. They were definitely popular but they weren’t pop. They wrote intelligent songs but with a fair share of technical bravado on their instruments and innovative yet tasteful sound engineering in the same vein of bands like Radiohead and Doves at the time. All old school Coldplay fans would probably share similar sentiments. Us Coldplay fans looked a lot similar to this when we were growing up. Modern Coldplay is an example of commercial pop music at its worst. Take away the sonic instrumental experimentation and instead put in electronic computer programmer loops and samples. Focus more on marketing, publicity and touring rather than on songwriting, innovation and simple band practicing. Throw in a bunch of cringey, force fed collaborations. Envision a basic formula for their craft and then multiply that formula by 300%. (Studio execs: ‘They’re a bit whiny. Let’s make that lead singer go Ohhh ohh ooo every five seconds. That's what the fans seem to like. And let ‘em write a a shitload of slow piano driven ballads. I think they're a woman's rock band. Let them have that guitar player repeating the same derivative chiming hook. In fact toss one of his hooks into the looping software and we'll rework it for an entire album. How about we let each one of them wear a different color? You know like the Spice Girls. Make it seem like they care about stuff around the world like climate change and fair trade and all that crap.’) This is what a modern day Coldplay fan kinda looks like. And that’s why some people don’t like Coldplay. In my humble opinion.

Text: What show / movie had no right to be as good as it was? Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. It wasn't the greatest of vacations because our cousin and her boyfriend were having these vicious fights over money (they weren't in the best place financially and had four daughters below the age of 5). We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive….but with a Woman. When The World Was Not Enough ended with its typical 007 sexual innuendo type final scene my brother and I looked at each other and nodded. It was ok. There was a lot of explosions, chase scenes, Denise Richards’ bouncing breasts and shorty shorts but we both knew we were unimpressed. However, in our typical peer influenced macho-vision we pretended that the movie was the real deal. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! We left the cinema thoroughly satisfied and entertained in so much that the choas that awaited us home didn't seem to matter anymore. I recently rewatched it with the idea that maybe it wasn't that great and maybe because we were dumb teenagers it had made an impression. I was blown away even moreso a thirty something year old dad than as a thirteen year old boy. The movie abandons every cliche there is about on-the-run and fugitive type action thrillers. The lead role is no superhero, there is no stupid forced comic relief character making racist jokes, there is no romantic subplot. Straight up escape and revenge served on a hot plate with Tommy Lee Jones in his best performance ever imho. I sincerely recommend it.

Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive\u2026.but with a Woman. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! Text: Which actor played a villain role too well for comfort? Ann Dowd as Joan in Hereditary. ***Spoiler Alert*** The performance by this relatively unknown actress blew me away and everyone who I've known to watch this film. Joan is the motherly figure who befriends Toni Collette's main character Annie who is going through a really tough time. Toni Collette's exemplary performance as a depressed middle aged mother suffering from tragedy is complimented by Ann Dowd's Joan who wins the heart of the viewers as a sympathetic, patient and caring matriarchal figure in the first half, only to suddenly transform into someone truly terrifying in the second half. What was scary for me about her performance was the genuine warmth she generated from the very moment she entered the screen. I can't see anyone being unable to put their guard down and love and accept this lady. It didn't seem like a performance at all. It seemed like that is how Ann Dowd really is. However when she lifts the veil it is almost bloodcurdling to see the transformation in her appearance and especially in her voice. Nothing is more scarier to me than evil people convincingly disguised as good and with that Ann Dowd truly delivered.

Text: What things do people say that make you roll your eyes? A guy from my neighbourhood came to my house some time ago asking for help. He had gotten a flat tire and wanted to borrow my spare for the following day as he needed to check out a job in the morning. From the moment we started speaking to the moment we parted, our conversation was a series of eye rolling on my part. Me: So how come you don't have a spare? Him: I just bought an amp and some speakers. Money’s finished. My car probably has the best music setup in the whole street. Me: (At his house) But look you have another car here. Why don't you use this car? Him: That car isn't working. Me: Then why don't you use one of the tires. It's the same size. Him: That's not my car that's my wife's. Wife (comes out to say hello, seemingly drunk): I have a car for sale. If you only see the engine on this car. Proceeds to open the hood on the car previously mentioned. Me: But is this car working? Wife: Who says it's not working? (glares at husband). Me: (Looking at the engine) Why are there sunflower seeds on top the carburetor? Wife: That damn parrot! It acts as if this car is his house. Husband: I'm actually a mechanic myself. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you can't fix your wife's car?’) Mmhmm. Husband: I have practically every tool there are for cars. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you don't have a spare tire.’) Mmhmm Husband: If ever you need work done on your car be sure to check me. Me: Will do. Husband: Can I borrow your tire wrench? I can't find mine. Husband: I can do masonry, plumbing, electrical, roofing. Wife: He's very talented. I never have to call anybody to get work done. I have an entire contracting company living in my house. Husband: Take my number. (He proceeds to search for a call card in his wallet but the area is in darkness.) Honey shine a light on my wallet for a second. Me: Why don't you put up some lights in the front yard? Husband: (Says nothing) Wife: (Scowling) The man just asked you a question. Husband: Well your spare didn't fit but thanks for the help anyway. Me: No problem. Husband: Can you do me one more favour? Me: (groaning) What? Husband: (Whispering so his wife, who went back in the house, doesn't hear). Can you lend me $20? I’ll need it for gas in the morning. Me: Sure (hands him a $20) Husband: (whispering even softer) You want a beer? Me: Yeah why not. Husband: If I go with you she'll know that I'm going for alcohol. You don't mind going to the grocery and getting it for us. (Hands me back my $20) Me: (Puts $20 back in wallet). Sure thing man. I then went home. I wonder how long he waited until it dawned on him that I was not coming back with his beers.

Text: What's the most ridiculous thing a coworker told on you to your boss for? At my very first job at 19 years old I was a warehouse attendant. I was a naturally friendly individual and honestly believed that it was my duty to try and befriend all of my coworkers on my first day of work. I wore glasses and have pretty bad eyesight. I had a talk with a guy named Duane. He wore thick glasses also and looked and acted exactly like Big Smoke from the video game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. I confided in him that my I was due for an eye test for new glasses. Duane had a ‘gangsta’ ideology about himself that made me feel awkward but I honestly believed I made a friend that day. His large, stocky friend Arnold who was even more provocative and blunt asked me to borrow $20 to buy lunch. I loaned him the money and humbly asked him to repay me the next day as I was low on cash. The following day I approached Arnold to get my $20 back because I needed it to buy lunch for myself. Arnold gets angry and makes a scene. He says that I'm trash because it hasn't even been 24 hrs and I'm harassing him for a measly $20. Duane chimes in and agrees with Arnold and chastises me for not understanding 'the game.’ Regardless I get my money back. An hour later the supervisor calls me in his office. He sits me down and tells me that he heard that my glasses are in need of a new prescription and that I have to get them changed according to Occupational Health and Safety law. I asked the supervisor if Duane told him this and he replied yes. The supervisor tells me that he's giving me a week to get proper prescribed glasses. I approached Duane and asked him why did he tell the supervisor something which I confided in him. I spoke in his language and asked him why he snitched on me. Duane replied that I crossed his boy Arnold by embarrassing him for the $20 he owed me so I qualified for being snitched on for my outdated glasses. Then there was silence. Such was the way of the gangsta. Duane snitched on my outdated glasses because I upset Arnold for publicly asking for my $20 back.

Text: What red flag did you have right before a job offer that you wish you had heeded? 'You’re really taking the job at that branch. I heard Ms. Khan is gonna be the manager there!’ There was a frenzied murmur among all the fellow workers of the branch of Mario's pizzeria that I worked in 2020. Ms. Khan was the name that could evoke the strongest emotions of fear, disgust and anger among most frontline staff. Back in 2020 I was strapped for cash and needed an extra source of income to complete my home after COVID had put a hold on everything for an entire year. I worked six years doing pizza delivery prior to this and for the most part it was not the most pleasant experience, especially when it's your evening job and you work 14 hrs a days, 7 days a week. On my little rickety old motorcycle I had been knocked down by drunken motorists, drenched up to my underwear with rain, cursed and threatened by irate customers, robbed at gunpoint and escaped near death collisions more times than I can count on one hand. I left the profession in 2019 with no intention of returning. However that wonderful virus called COVID had me putting on that old red shirt and dusting the old helmet, feeling akin to George Foreman when he took another stab at boxing in his middle ages to pay off his debts. The only redeeming factor was a branch was going to be opened practically next door to where I lived. I wouldn't be stranded late at nights trying to get a taxi home like was the case before. Fast forward to my first day at work at the new branch next to my home. I'm introduced to the dreaded Ms. Khan. I see this lady with a soft, lusty voice, enigmatic brown eyes and huge boobs shake my hands. She looked only a few years older than me (34 at the time) and being a hot blooded, average Joe male I told myself she couldn't be all that bad. I couldn't be more wrong. I never saw someone conduct a meeting whereby they refused to hear any concerns staff had. She simply discussed what she wanted staff to do/not do and made obvious allusions as to who f**ked up for the month. I whispered to my fellow delivery driver that this wasn't a meeting, this was a briefing. With her eerily accentuated sense of hearing Ms. Khan heard me murmuring and angrily asked if I had any problems. I mentioned that I never saw a meeting conducted where staff wasn't allowed to express their concerns and I saw those enigmatic brown eyes stare at me as though I were the spawn of Satan. She ignored me and continued her meeting (briefing). From that moment on my relationship with Ms. Khan became tense to say the least. I observed that she had not the slightest concern to Industrial Law and the basic rights of workers and took advantage of the more naive workers to an almost sickening degree. I witnessed her telling a cashier who was about to finish shift that she couldn't leave because the other cashier couldn't make it. The cashier protested and said she had her two kids home with a babysitter who was leaving in a few minutes. Ms. Khan told her that if she leaved, consider her job gone. After Ms. Khan left I explained to that cashier that she could not be forced to work a double shift and Ms. Khan did not have the authority to fire and the company would dare not do as such under such conditions otherwise the company could have an ugly lawsuit on their hands. The cashier was grateful for my advice and left. Ms. Khan was the forced to take up her role as cashier for that evening. Ms. Khan got wind that I had advised the cashier her rights. From that moment on it became a cold war between Ms. Khan and myself. She became obsessed with my roster and if I came two minutes lates she etched bold red letters in the time book of my 'constant and unapologetic tardiness. ‘ She sent me home if my trousers had a spot of dirt on it, despite it being well known that motorcycle delivery riders always get their trousers dirty due to the nature of the job. Other drivers would perform their duty in filthy and worn trousers but none of that angered Ms. Khan than a tiny ink stain on my trousers. Ms. Khan was obsessed with sales targets. Sales targets gave her cash bonuses and everyone began to witness she had a tendency to employ dirty tactics to get customers to spend more money. These tactics employed fraud and dishonesty and several customers grew wise to it. Some of them began complaining to me about being cheated. Whenever I approached Ms. Khan about these complaints she dismissed me and accused me being the Devil's Advocate. However one fateful day one of these customers sent an angry email to the head office about the scheme and Ms. Khan's name was called. She flew into a fit of paranoia and began to accuse me trying to 'get the customers against’ her.’ She started gathering a bunch of her manager friends from other branches and (according to my fellow deliver drivers) she spread the rumour that I was a pompous chauvinist that didn't like to see women in charge. I got wind that she held meetings while I was at my day job, telling the (mostly female) staff that I was a dangerous defiant, possibly a spy for Pizza Hut and that I was racist, sexist (all the ‘ists in the dictionary) and didn't care if the women employed here lost their jobs. Sounds ridiculous but sadly when you have an organization of which 80% of the frontline staff barely have elementary education and are fearful of losing their bread and butter, such scare tactics actually do work. I was watched upon with suspicion as a dishonest rabble rouser who wanted the company to fail and who stood to lose nothing because I already had a day job. Suddenly everything I said was reported to the manager and every disagreement I had with fellow workers was blown out of proportion. Every time I gave basic legal advice to a stressed out single mother being taken advantage of, someone was in the background reporting my 'insubordination’ to Ms. Khan. Many times I was called to the head office to defend myself and remind them of my great work ethic and relationship with the customers, while Ms. Khan repeated 'insubordination’ and 'I feel uncomfortable with him ’ like an dull parrot. The atmosphere became so tense that when my contract came to an end and I was informed by the head office that it would not be renewed. I grew angry and wanted to take the matter up legally but then I realized it was a gift from God. My home was near finished. Working in that branch was making me constantly angry, shocked and disappointed at how easily people get themselves taken advantaged of and how people like Ms. Khan take advantage of others with no remorse. Nothings screams the decline of an organisation more than when taking advantage of customers become the norm and something only becomes illegal/unethical if you are caught. It's been over a year since I stopped working there and I've never been happier. I advise anyone going through similar problems in their workplace to make that great effort to get out of there. A toxic work environment WILL make you a toxic person. If you are able to make that effort to leave, do it right now. Believe me. It's not the end of the world and it's worth it.

Text: What is an unpopular opinion you hold? Self-Help Books Can Actually Ruin Your Life Especially if you come from a developing country. Have you ever sat and pondered as to the staggering amount of self-help authors there are out there? It seems every week someone is recommending to you some brand new, groundbreaking, best selling title that eschews a whole new perspective on how to view the world and live your life. The problem with 99% of the authors: Are they really living their dreams? Or are they making a living selling dreams? Moulding a life of success, solely based on easily digestible tips, hints and formulae is like solving advanced level algebra, whilst riding a roller coaster, using only your knowledge of multiplication tables. The knowledge can help….you probably might get the most simple problems correct……but it would be ridiculous to think that you would be able to solve all your problems in that manner, under those unique circumstances. These are people living in dire poverty in India. What can I do to help them out of this financial rut?….. I know! Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill A lonely, mentally unhinged taxi driver… That's easy. The Road Less Travelled and How to Win Friends and Influence People. A wealthy but socially and emotionally void and suicidal philanthropist. Hmm. That's a tough one….The Alchemist by Paolo Coelho and you can throw in The Prophet by Gibran as well. Nothing cures rich-man depression more than obscure but romanticised Eastern parables and fables. Ok, so it's foolish to try and live according to a self help book, but how can I ruin my life simply by seeking advice? In every job that I've worked, every year there's always that one newly employed guy who is all jacked up from reading a lifetime's supply of self help books. He is always brimming with confidence and eager to pin his obstacles against the ropes and send failure scattering with his 2000 watt grin. He hates to hear no and scorns to see people second guessing themselves. He wants to take on all life's challenges and has a Napoleon Hill or Robert Kiyosaki quote ready for every situation. Then something inexplicable happens. Something gradually builds up, registers in his subconscious and overflows upon his ego. It usually takes the form of this mental conversation. 'Wait a minute. I've done everything the book advised me to. I've followed the instructions to the hilt…….yet I'm not seeing the results.’ He hasn't been promoted by his supervisor, rather his supervisor has been taking credit for his own efforts and is getting the promotion instead. Despite constantly showing support and empathy, his wife is even more nagging and helpless than when he first met her. His dedication to go above and beyond with the customer now has him doing the workload of all the lazy and incompetent coworkers around him, who still draw the same salary. He gets the lion's share of verbal abuse from disgruntled customers who rather voice their issues with him rather than the incompetent coworkers. His small business as a landscaper is suffering because his fair price is being exploited whilst mediocre landscapers are charging abominably overpriced rates and are getting more work than him. What the hell is happening here? He followed some great and timeless advice. He just forget to put in one small factor in his equation. His personal environment. His ever changing, ever complex, personal environment. The variable that if included onto his scientific calculator would produce the answer E or 'Error.’ In developing countries likes Trinidad, using US or English or German translated or Dutch translated or any developed country self help books can cause ruin your life because the environment is so different. In developing countries: These are all factors that contradict with what he read in his books and come only through experience. Had he been all the wiser he would've known that not every bit of advice in his self help books could be applied to his unique situation and environment. To make matters worse nowadays, everybody is a self help author and rather than have synchronized, compatible, time tested advice, we have polarising, wishy-washy, one-size-fits-all concoctions and psudo-psychological, parabolic gibberish. Basically, self help authors write anecdotes that's easy to understand, easy to apply and appealing to the majority. Below is a list of a few popular modern self help authors and their most famous philosophy: Robert Kiyosaki: If you have to lose, lose spectacularly. Malcolm Gladwell: You have within you an instinct to know when something 'feels’ like a rip-off. Jay Shetty: Think like a monk. Deepak Chopak: Thinking is like brain chemistry. Steve Harvey: Act like a lady, think like a man Paolo Coelho: The universe…

Text: What is that one picture that describes the lowest point in your life? Sometime in April 2015 I used to be one of those who believed that depression was a hackneyed excuse, lazy people used as a defence mechanism. I believed that any mental struggle could be conquered on a mind-over-matter basis. My extended family was prone to bouts of depression and bipolar disorder and I would always roll my eyes when I heard them speak of their troubles and how it has affected their lives. At age 28 my girlfriend became pregnant. It was not planned. Prior to this announcement we were sharing a modest apartment and no matter how much I tightened my belt I couldn't overcome experiencing great financial difficulties. Besides my day job I also got an income doing transport and lawn maintenance. Soon my vehicle started giving me no end of troubles and I could no longer spend money fixing it so I left it to rot. My credit card was maxed out and I was owing money to some of my friends. After paying rent I could barely afford groceries. My financial woes caused me to lose contact with my friends so when she and I argued (which was every week) and she stormed out, I was left destitute and lonely in a shabby apartment complex, no one and nowhere to turn. During one of these episodes, like an awful aftertaste, a notion came into my mind. You've made a big mistake. You're going to f**k this child's life up . I tried to laugh away the notion but it buzzed around my mind like some sort of devilish fairy. You’re just another deadbeat father who can't get it right. I started pacing around trying to get this notion out of my mind. My heart raced and my nerves were on edge. My head felt light and heavy at the same time. You've made such a big mistake. What the hell were you thinking? I took deep breaths and attempted to think positive thoughts. Then as though a floodgate was released, it came: panic attacks. I felt these strange sensations in my skin, these popping, spasmic sensations similar to the plastic bubbles that wrap your delivery that you pop unconsciously with your fingers. It was completely overwhelming. I sat down to try and breathe it away, mind-over-matter as I used to preach but it simply gave way to what I can only describe as the feeling of a heavy, stifling bog taking residence in my brain. It was depression. My back hunched over as my mind felt clogged and lifeless. I couldn't stop thinking of my problems and asking myself interrogative questions. I sat down in defeat, fearful for anyone to see me like this, fearful for the phone to ring. The worst thing about depression is that it tricks you into believing that your life was always a series of tragedy and sorrow, that this is how things are and has always been. It was as though my positive emotions and memories were locked away in a cellar, unrecognizable in an iron mask. I felt like a burden and a drain on other people's happiness. When I saw other people happy and proactive it only reminded me of how unhappy and useless I was. These sensations would usually happen during sunsets for some strange reason. My appetite was all but gone so was my passions and interests. At its peak I became emaciated, 30–40 pounds lighter than my usual self. This feeling came on a daily basis, first with a dose of panic attacks then sinking into that low, rotting, depressed feeling where my face literally looked like Eeyore from Winnie the Pooh. I would record my suicidal feelings on a rating from 1 to 10 and on many days I would record myself as high as 9. After my daughter was born I was terrified of getting the male version of post partum depression. Thankfully, I was lucky, the depression wasn't chronic and it waned to a point where only once a week I got those horrid familiar feelings but of a lesser intensity. After a year I was healthy enough to take up a second job, clear my debts and provide for my daughter whilst my mental demons were held at bay. Today, I am in a much better place mentally and financially. Not going to brag but I think I've accomplished a bit since depression first reared its ugly head seven years ago. However, it's comes back every now and again. Like a unwanted vagabond it shows up at my doorstep, bedraggled and defeated, but not yet dead and it stops me in my tracks to give me a taste of those familiar feelings of the past, (usually during sunsets). Depression is no joke. If you know someone who demonstrates any symptoms/behaviours such as I had/did, try your best to assist that person, without overwhelming them with pity and making a huge fuss. Be patient with such a person without coming across as though they are helpless. Just play it cool. Edit 21.01.22. Depression and other mental illnesses play a great role in relationships and with families. It is very difficult to be in a relationship with a spouse who suffers from mental illness. It can cause severe problems for future generations. Click here to read how it.

Text: Whom did you feel bad for in high school? Balram. There was a boy who came from the depths of poverty named Balram. He was sinewy and had coarse skin and features that made him look like he jumped out of the pages of our history books as an indentured laborer from colonial times. Everything about him was out of sync with the rest of the class. This was the late 90s and baggy pants were the thing, Balram wore his khaki trousers wrapped tight around his skinny legs. Perms from excessive hair gel (my specialty at the time), corn-rows, Caesar styled and spiky hair was the rage amongst teenage boys back then. Balram wore something that looked straight out of a an old Amitabh Bachchan movie from the 70s. Balram's school uniforms always looked faded and threadbare. Never once did anyone see him wearing new items of clothing. This led to many of the kids in class poking fun at the possibility that Balram's family got used clothes for him. Balram didn't have cable. It was possible he didn't have a TV. Balram didn't care for the music everyone else listened to. He didn't go to the arcade and play video games. He didn't get excited hearing about Stone Cold Steve Austin. He was odd in that he only enjoyed games that demonstrated his eerie strength and his skills in survival. This included holding breath competitions, arm wrestling, 'mercy’ and 'bokee' (hitting an opponents fist by flicking a finger against it until someone gives up in pain). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He would sit in class like an old Native American chief, peering knowingly at the world through his squinted, Charles Bronson-esque eyes while everyone else made jokes and acted like morons who needed attention. My friends and I would hang out with him but for some reason he never was an official member of our group. He preferred to roam alone. Once, I was tricked by some boys into pretending to want to beat him up, all for kicks. Before I could say 'Hey' Balram lifted me into the air by the shoulders and against the wall until I yielded. It was an impressive display of brute strength that I could never forget. In moments of boredom Balram was usually an easy target for jokes and insults. Some of the girls were particularly mean to him. One would say to that she would never be with a boy like him who looks dirty and always smells like old curry. The boys would always joke around that he came from 'the bush’ and came to school swinging on vines like Tarzan. One of the boys even managed to create a comic depicting Balram's life in the bush, fighting snakes and tigers on a daily basis etc. Balram learned to laugh with everyone and not let it get to him. In Form 3 Balram vanished. Always a recluse he never communicated to anyone what were his plans/intentions. Some months later he visited the school wearing a new uniform and with a friend at his side. He got transferred to a school closer to home where more rural kids like him were around. He looked much happier and was far more social than he was before. That day, most of the class ignored him but my friends and I held a reception to commemorate the good times we had with him. He said his new school was the best; teachers were hardly there and the kids did what they wanted. He showed me a tattoo that he got on his arm of a dragon. Even though the tattoo looked ridiculously amateurish and his clothes were still faded and threadbare and his hair still outdated my friends and I sang his praises and gave him his day. He really was a great guy. He had no fear of trying to fit in and had an infinite amount of patience for those around him. I wouldn't be surprised to find out that he made a huge success out if his life as an adult. But alas that day was the last time I saw him/heard anything about him.

"Whom did you feel bad for in high school? Balram. There was a boy who came from the depths of poverty named Balram. He was sinewy and had coarse skin and features that made him look like he jumped out of the pages of our history books as an indentured laborer from colonial times. Everything about him was out of sync with the rest of the class. This was the late 90s and baggy pants were the thing, Balram wore his khaki trousers wrapped tight around his skinny legs. Perms from excessive hair gel (my specialty at the time), corn-rows, Caesar styled and spiky hair was the rage amongst teenage boys back then. Balram wore something that looked straight out of a an old Amitabh Bachchan movie from the 70s. Balram's school uniforms always looked faded and threadbare. Never once did anyone see him wearing new items of clothing. This led to many of the kids in class poking fun at the possibility that Balram's family got used clothes for him. Balram didn't have cable. It was possible he didn't have a TV. Balram didn't care for the music everyone else listened to. He didn't go to the arcade and play video games. He didn't get excited hearing about Stone Cold Steve Austin. He was odd in that he only enjoyed games that demonstrated his eerie strength and his skills in survival. This included holding breath competitions, arm wrestling, 'mercy\u2019 and 'bokee' (hitting an opponents fist by flicking a finger against it until someone gives up in pain). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He would sit in class like an old Native American chief, peering knowingly at the world through his squinted, Charles Bronson-esque eyes while everyone else made jokes and acted like morons who needed attention. My friends and I would hang out with him but for some reason he never was an official member of our group. He preferred to roam alone. Once, I was tricked by some boys into pretending to want to beat him up, all for kicks. Before I could say 'Hey' Balram lifted me into the air by the shoulders and against the wall until I yielded. It was an impressive display of brute strength that I could never forget. In moments of boredom Balram was usually an easy target for jokes and insults. Some of the girls were particularly mean to him. One would say to that she would never be with a boy like him who looks dirty and always smells like old curry. The boys would always joke around that he came from 'the bush\u2019 and came to school swinging on vines like Tarzan. One of the boys even managed to create a comic depicting Balram's life in the bush, fighting snakes and tigers on a daily basis etc. Balram learned to laugh with everyone and not let it get to him. In Form 3 Balram vanished. Always a recluse he never communicated to anyone what were his plans/intentions. Some months later he visited the school wearing a new uniform and with a friend at his side. He got transferred to a school closer to home where more rural kids like him were around. He looked much happier and was far more social than he was before. That day, most of the class ignored him but my friends and I held a reception to commemorate the good times we had with him. He said his new school was the best; teachers were hardly there and the kids did what they wanted. He showed me a tattoo that he got on his arm of a dragon. Text: Which supporting actress was much more memorable than the star of a movie? Toni Collette gave one of the greatest performances ever rendered on film in the soon to be cult classic Hereditary (2018) but another actress outshined her by a fraction of a fraction. Ann Dowd gave a most chillingly deceptive performance of Joan, a warm and empathetic older lady who befriends Collette's character Annie as she struggles with tragedy, resentment and depression. The beauty of Ann's performance is her complex nuances. She transforms from a lovable, nurturing Aunt May type character that was so understated yet genuinely compassionate to a different being one would've never predicted her to be near the ending. The most common description I've heard about her character for those who've enjoyed the film is how 'real’ Joan seemed. Ann Dowd is one of the most underrated actresses of the 21st century. No one can play matriarchal type figures like her and even the most hardened scoundrel would find themselves letting down their guards and engaging a sense of love and trust in the warmth she emanates. Therefore it's startling when that different side of her comes out during the final 20 minutes of the film. I'm not giving spoilers because YOU NEED TO GO SEE HEREDITARY IF YOU HAVENT SEEN IT YET.

Text: What is the scariest moment you have had in your own home? This is a roughly 6 feet deep hole that I had dug in my front yard some years ago. It is dug to insert an electrical power pole and concrete and stones are poured to keep it in place. Doesn't it seem like a fun idea to play Rambo and jump in such a hole, cover it with dead leaves and braches and jump out to scare anyone who visits you? That's just the movies and no I did not do anything so silly. But in reality, you could possibly die by jumping into a narrow 6 feet deep hole. I say this because it almost happened to me: Here in the Tropics we have the dry season and the rainy season. I don't think I need to explain the difference. However in the rainy season we tend to get what is called the Hurricane season which is a period that characterizes long and heavy rain, thunderstorms and the occasional flash flood. My area is prone to flooding. This a view of my front yard and the road during an average Hurricane Season flood. (The pole at the center-right is where the hole was located.) My hole was dug during the dry season. However the not-too-wholesome electrician I hired who was to put in the pole delayed the job for months upon months until hurricane season reached. One day, I heard a faint squeaking noise coming from the hole. I looked in to see a cute little mouse fighting to survive in the 8 inches of water that remained in the hole due to rain. I couldn't help but feel sorry for the little bugger so I grabbed a piece of wood and stretched it towards it, thinking the mouse would gladly hop onto the wood and allow me to save him. It turns out the mouse would rather take its chances drowning. I had half the mind to leave the stupid creature to drown but my heart got the better of me and I decided to jump in and fetch the mouse by hand. I got in, carefully avoiding stepping on the creature. It was quite muddy at the base and hard to move because it was mostly clay. I picked up the little mouse and carefully extended my hand out of the hole and dropped him lightly on the surface where I would assume he scuttled off in great appreciation of me. I then tried hoisting myself out. However the entire area was slippery due to last night's showers. I couldn't get a good grip on anything due to the slipperiness, the lack of room to maneuver and because my feet kept getting stuck deep in the mud where I stood. I tried for several times but to no avail. I had no idea that this little hole would be such a challenge. Mind you I'm only 5’ 10 and don't have the wingspan of Michael Phelps. Regardless if I did, everywhere I gripped my hand slid on the clay mud. After several attempts my energy was depleted. Suddenly thunder boomed and a heavy rain started. My heart began to pulse. I realized that I could quite possibly drown here; if not from the rain filling this hole up then the possible flood afterwards. I yelled for help a few times but to no luck, the sound of heavy rain was competing with my yells. The only chance of anyone hearing me was if someone happened to be walking the road nearby. What are the chances of someone casually walking the road during a thunderstorm? I had to get out of this simple hole or drown like my mouse friend almost did. What a dumb way to die I might add. The water level in the hole was beginning to rise towards my knees. In a frenzied fit of desperation I found some reserve of energy and my brain started to click. I undid my mud soaked shoes which was causing additional heaviness, threw them out and like a cat on steroids I simply grabbed and flailed at the four walls with my hands, feet and back until I somehow managed to get a grip and lift myself out. Some fingers and parts of my back were bleeding from contact with sharp stones. I looked as though I just survived D-Day Normandy when all I did was come out of a small, muddy hole; an idiot who almost died saving a mouse. So take it from me if you want to live a long fulfilling life. Don't jump into muddy 6 feet deep holes, especially during Hurricane season. Edit: Wow I'm actually getting upvotes for this. You all care about my life. That's sweet. Here is another mouse (or could very well be the same one) I befriended during a flood a few weeks later. Edit 2: Many commenters are suggesting that I should've simply allowed the water in the hole to rise and simply float/paddle my way to the surface. Please. By all means, if this bizarre situation ever happens to you do not wait for that possibility. This wasn't a tiled pool but a muddy hole more narrow than a coffin. You can drown trying to free your feet from the thick, viscous clay mud that envelops your feet and the fact that your arms and legs have limited motion. Scream for help as best as you can and if that fails get your arse out of that hole by whatever means but do not wait for the water to rise on you. You might as well be buried there the following day.

This is a roughly 6 feet deep hole that I had dug in my front yard some years ago. It is dug to insert an electrical power pole and concrete and stones are poured to keep it in place. That's just the movies and no I did not do anything so silly. But in reality, you could possibly die by jumping into a narrow 6 feet deep hole. I say this because it almost happened to me: Here in the Tropics we have the dry season and the rainy season. I don't think I need to explain the difference. However in the rainy season we tend to get what is called the Hurricane season which is a period that characterizes long and heavy rain, thunderstorms and the occasional flash flood. My area is prone to flooding. This a view of my front yard and the road during an average Hurricane Season flood. (The pole at the center-right is where the hole was located.) My hole was dug during the dry season. However the not-too-wholesome electrician I hired who was to put in the pole delayed the job for months upon months until hurricane season reached. One day, I heard a faint squeaking noise coming from the hole. I looked in to see a cute little mouse fighting to survive in the 8 inches of water that remained in the hole due to rain. I couldn't help but feel sorry for the little bugger so I grabbed a piece of wood and stretched it towards it, thinking the mouse would gladly hop onto the wood and allow me to save him. It turns out the mouse would rather take its chances drowning. I had half the mind to leave the stupid creature to drown but my heart got the better of me and I decided to jump in and fetch the mouse by hand. I got in, carefully avoiding stepping on the creature. It was quite muddy at the base and hard to move because it was mostly clay. I picked up the little mouse and carefully extended my hand out of the hole and dropped him lightly on the surface where I would assume he scuttled off in great appreciation of me. I then tried hoisting myself out. However the entire area was slippery due to last night's showers. I couldn't get a good grip on anything due to the slipperiness, the lack of room to maneuver and because my feet kept getting stuck deep in the mud where I stood. I tried for several times but to no avail. I had no idea that this little hole would be such a challenge. Mind you I'm only 5\u2019 10 and don't have the wingspan of Michael Phelps. Regardless if I did, everywhere I gripped my hand slid on the clay mud. After several attempts my energy was depleted. Suddenly thunder boomed and a heavy rain started. My heart began to pulse. I realized that I could quite possibly drown here; if not from the rain filling this hole up then the possible flood afterwards. I yelled for help a few times but to no luck, the sound of heavy rain was competing with my yells. The only chance of anyone hearing me was if someone happened to be walking the road nearby. What are the chances of someone casually walking the road during a thunderstorm? I had to get out of this simple hole or drown like my mouse friend almost did. What a dumb way to die I might add. Jackson in mind for the role in Pulp Fiction. It is truly the role Jackson was born to play. It is the role that took Jackson into stardom and to this day Jules’ intimidating obscenity ridden threats, interrogation, debates on burgers and pork, not to mention his love of quoting Ezekiel 25:17 is constantly memed, quoted and parodied. But I wouldn't consider Jackson a great actor. He may sit more comfortable with his tough guy roles but he isn't anywhere near the range of other legendary tough guy actors like Denzel Washington, Clint Eastwood and James Cagney. If you know Jackson is going to be in a movie you are certain that he isn't going to be a bespectacled data programmer hunched behind a computer or a main love interest. He is probably the most famous typecast of Hollywood film history since John Wayne. It's a bit unfortunate because when he attempts more vulnerable or intellectual characters it comes across as forgettable at best and eerie at worst in my honest opinion (Tarzan, RoboCop, Star Wars). I don't think Sam may get another role as defining and well written as Jules in Pulp Fiction. I think a large portion of his filmography isn't impressive from an acting standpoint. He may not be a Marlon Brando or a Laurence Olivier but neither of them could've put in the heart and energy into an intricately moulded character such as Jules Winnfield.
